name: Hard-to-Borrow Reversal (Borrow-Income Trade)
summary: Short the stock and buy a synthetic long (long call, short put, same strike and expiry) so the price exposure cancels, leaving the stock-loan rebate on the short position as the income - the trade market makers actually run, as distinct from the pricing arbitrage the bank already lists as a Reversal.

legs.strike_rule: short 100 shares of a hard-to-borrow name
legs.dte_rule: held for the life of the options

legs.strike_rule: the same strike K, same expiry - together with the long call this is a synthetic long share position

max_profit: The borrow rebate earned over the holding period, less the options' net cost and any dividends owed - a carry, not a payoff
max_loss: In principle small and defined, because the synthetic long exactly offsets the short shares. In practice: an early assignment on the short put, a borrow recall and forced buy-in, a dividend surprise, or a rebate rate cut - each of which can exceed the entire expected income.
breakevens: None in price terms; the trade breaks even when the accrued rebate equals the options' net cost plus financing
typical_dte: 30-90 DTE, rolled while the borrow stays special
when_to_use: INCLUDED FOR COMPLETENESS - NOT TRADEABLE ON THIS ACCOUNT. Documented so the distinction between the bank's pricing-arbitrage Reversal and the market maker's income trade is explicit: the first harvests a mispriced put-call parity, the second harvests the stock-loan market.
entry_rules: BLOCKED, for two independent reasons. First, the short put alongside a short stock position requires level 4 approval. Second, and decisively: retail brokerage accounts including Alpaca do not pass stock-loan rebates through to the customer, so the income this trade exists to capture does not reach this account at all.
If it were ever enabled: borrow rebate must exceed 10% annualized and be contractually confirmed for a stated term, not quoted intraday.
Options must price at or better than parity, so the structure is not paying away the rebate in option edge.
No ex-dividend date inside the holding period - the short seller owes every dividend in cash.
Name must not be on a threshold or hard-to-borrow recall watchlist.
management_rules: Monitor the borrow rate daily; unwind the moment the rebate falls below the cost of carrying the options.
Never let the synthetic drift from the share count - 100 shares per 1 call / 1 put, exactly.
Unwind all three legs as a single package, never piecemeal.
exit_rules: ASSIGNMENT GUARD: the short put is assignable at any time; flatten it by 15:30 ET on expiration day and immediately at extrinsic < $0.10 or |delta| >= 0.85. Assignment buys 100 shares and closes the short, ending the rebate stream without warning.
Close the long call rather than exercising it.
Unwind immediately on any borrow recall notice - a forced buy-in in a hard-to-borrow name is the most expensive event in this structure.
Never carry the position through an ex-dividend date.
assignment_risk: Two ways to lose the position involuntarily: early assignment on the short put, and a stock-loan recall forcing a buy-in of the short shares. Both terminate the trade at the counterparty's choosing, which is the opposite of what a carry trade needs.
buying_power: Reg-T short stock margin (150% of proceeds) plus the option requirements. Level 4.
liquidity_needs: Hard-to-borrow names are by definition thin in both the share and option markets - the least liquid setting in the bank.
common_mistakes: Confusing it with the listed Reversal (a pricing arb, closed the moment parity restores) when this one is held for weeks to accrue carry; assuming a retail account receives any part of the lending revenue; ignoring the dividend obligation.
family: Completeness gap-fill (cross-family): ratio/naked-financed put and call structures, quantity-unbalanced condors and strangles, stock+option overlays and monetizations, capital-protection and hybrid builds, 0DTE four-leg income, volatility-surface and relative-value trades, event-driven overlays, and roll/adjustment structures
blocked_because: needs Alpaca options level 4; this account is level 3. Alpaca rejects it with 'account not eligible to trade uncovered option contracts'. Raising the level is an Alpaca approval, not a code change.
